item.title: Zelenskiy Says US Looks for Deal Ending Russia’s War by June
item.description: Ukraine’s President Volodymyr Zelenskiy says the US is proposing to finish all necessary negotiations to end Russia’s invasion of Ukraine in June.

item.title: Charting the Global Economy: ECB Holds, UK Tilts Toward Rate Cut
item.description: The European Central Bank left interest rates unchanged, while President Christine Lagarde downplayed a recent rally in the euro and maintained that inflation as broadly balanced.

item.title: ACC Ends Germany, Italy Factories as Stellantis Retreats on EVs
item.description: Automotive Cells Co. confirmed it will halt plans to build battery gigafactories in Germany and Italy and said it is holding talks with unions at its French venture as key backer Stellantis NV downsizes its electric-vehicle plans.

item.title: Wild Week of Trading Leaves Pockmarks Across US Equity Landscape
item.description: Precious metals memed out, Bitcoin flamed out and the labor market looks like it’s petering out. None of it started in the equities market, but together it was enough — along with a reckoning for software firms — to shake the foundation of an AI-driven bull run.

item.title: Rising Fire Risk Prompts Utilities to Deliberately Cut Power
item.description: Data, technology and human judgment help US power companies consider when to turn off transmission lines.

item.title: Tech’s AI Push Risks a Bond Market Blowback: Credit Weekly
item.description: The biggest tech companies are gearing up to spend even more on artificial intelligence than investors had anticipated, and money managers increasingly fear that whatever happens, credit markets will get hit.

item.title: Get Ready for Double Whammy of US Jobs and Inflation
item.description: Investors and policymakers are gearing up for a busy week of US economic reports that includes arguably the two most consequential data snapshots — employment and inflation.

item.title: Malaysia Draws First Data Center Protest Over Pollution, Water
item.description: The rapid increase in data centers in Malaysia came under the microscope on Saturday, with the AI-driven buildout drawing its first public protest in the Southeast Asian country.
